# Independent fixed scroll CLI oracle

Captured with unchanged `rust/tools/check_ui_scroll.py` and
`rust/tools/check_ui_scroller.py`, pinned CPython 3.12.15, Linux x86_64.
The provenance JSON files record interpreter/source hashes and the actual NumPy
2.5.3 extension used by the scroller source. This is not ARM equivalence proof.

The three scroll scenes contain all 4,500 original ordered frames; the three
scroller scenes contain all 720 original ordered frames. Inputs, source output,
and per-scene DEBUG_SCROLL=1 stdout were generated by the original Python
classes, independently of the Rust candidate. `integrity.json` pins compressed
and uncompressed bytes. `source-pins.json` and the complete NumPy lock record
make the native fixed oracle reject changed source/dependency contracts.

`failures.json` contains 85 executions of the whole unchanged original scripts
against real controlled child executables. It records exit status, child calls,
stdout hashes, and every resulting artifact's bytes/hash. Content-addressed
`blobs` include candidate replies and original debug/failure stdout. Cases cover
both strict scroll bounds, the inclusive scroller bound, recursive key/list
rules, Python boolean/numeric comparisons, decoder depth, strict UTF-8 and
universal newlines, late failures, stale outputs and debug prefixes. `cli.json`
contains 18 independent original argparse admissions and errors.

These native commands replace the fixed-input CI gates only. Source execution
failures due to importing/interpreting Python are intentionally replaced by
explicit source/dependency/corpus-integrity checks. The original generic UI
classes and arbitrary-input helpers remain separate pending runtime conversion;
this corpus does not implement their general input generation capability.

`actual-proof.json` records 16 whole original/native CLI comparisons using freshly
built current Rust `scroll_trace` and `scroller_trace` examples. Every artifact
and stdout byte matched. Cases include DEBUG_SCROLL values `0`, `1`, `01`, and
raw `ff`; raw Unix root alias/candidate/output names; and a child-verified inherited
raw environment value. Candidate/checker binary hashes are recorded per run.
